sanskrit: upetya cainam uvāca mā rājan krodhavaśaṃ gamaḥ prasādaṃ kuru nārhasi maṇḍūkānām anaparādhināṃ vadhaṃ kartum iti
english: Approaching him, he said: 'Do not, O king, fall under the sway of anger. Be gracious — you ought not to slay frogs who have committed no offense.'

sanskrit: mā maṇḍūkāñ jighāṃsa tvaṃ kopaṃ saṃdhārayācyuta ślokau cātra bhavataḥ prakṣīyete dhanodreko janānām avijānatām
english: 'Do not seek to kill the frogs; restrain your rage, O Acyuta. And in this regard two verses will be cited for you: the pride of wealth wanes for people who are ignorant.'

sanskrit: pratijānīhi naitāṃs tvaṃ prāpya krodhaṃ vimokṣyase alaṃ kṛtvā tavādharmaṃ maṇḍūkaiḥ kiṃ hatair hi te
english: 'Promise that, even upon encountering them again, you will not loose your anger. You have already done enough wrong — what, indeed, is to be gained by killing the frogs?'

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinam iṣṭajanaśokaparītātmā rājā provāca na hi kṣamyate tan mayā haniṣyāmy etān etair durātmabhiḥ priyā me bhakṣitā sarvathaiva me vadhyā maṇḍūkāḥ nārhasi vidvan mām uparoddhum iti
english: To him speaking thus, the king — his soul overwhelmed with grief for his beloved — replied: 'I cannot forgive this. I will kill them. By these evil-souled creatures my beloved was devoured; the frogs are in every way deserving of death. You should not, O learned one, obstruct me.'

sanskrit: sa tad vākyam upalabhya vyathitendriyamanāḥ provāca prasīda rājan aham āyur nāma maṇḍūkarājaḥ mama sā duhitā suśobhanā nāma tasyā dauḥśīlyam etat bahavo hi rājānas tayā vipralabdhapūrvā iti
english: He, hearing that speech, with senses and mind distressed, said: 'Be appeased, O king. I am Āyus, king of the frogs. That daughter of mine is named Suśobhanā. This is her bad conduct — many kings have been deceived by her before.'

sanskrit: tam abravīd rājā tayāsmy arthī sā me dīyatām iti
english: The king said to him: 'It is she I desire; let her be given to me.'

sanskrit: athaināṃ rājñe pitādāt abravīc cainām enaṃ rājānaṃ śuśrūṣasveti
english: Then her father gave her to the king, and said to her: 'Serve this king obediently.'

sanskrit: sa uvāca duhitaram yasmāt tvayā rājāno vipralabdhās tasmād abrahmaṇyāni tavāpatyāni bhaviṣyanty anṛtakatvāt taveti
english: He said to his daughter: 'Because you have deceived kings, your offspring will be hostile to Brahmins, on account of your untruthfulness.'

sanskrit: sa ca rājā tām upalabhya tasyāṃ surataguṇanibaddhahṛdayo lokatrayaiśvaryam ivopalabhya harṣabāṣpakalayā vācā praṇipatyābhipūjya maṇḍūkarājānam abravīt anugṛhīto 'smīti
english: The king, having received her, his heart bound by the virtues of their union as if he had obtained sovereignty over the three worlds, with a voice trembling with tears of joy, bowing down and honoring the king of frogs, said: 'I have been blessed.'

sanskrit: sa ca maṇḍūkarājo jāmātaram anujñāpya yathāgatam agacchat
english: And the king of frogs, having taken leave of his son-in-law, departed as he had come.

sanskrit: atha kasya cit kālasya tasyāṃ kumārās trayas tasya rājñaḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ śalo dalo balaś ceti tatas teṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ śalaṃ samaye pitā rājye 'bhiṣicya tapasi dhṛtātmā vanaṃ jagāma
english: After some time, three princes were born to that king by her — Śala, Dala, and Bala. Then, in due course, the father consecrated the eldest, Śala, in the kingdom, and with resolute mind departed to the forest for austerities.

sanskrit: atha kadā cic chalo mṛgayām acarat mṛgaṃ cāsādya rathenānvadhāvat
english: Once, Śala went hunting, and having sighted a deer, gave chase in his chariot.

sanskrit: sūtaṃ covāca śīghraṃ māṃ vahasveti
english: He said to the charioteer: 'Drive me swiftly!'

sanskrit: sa tathoktaḥ sūto rājānam abravīt mā kriyatām anubandhaḥ naiṣa śakyas tvayā mṛgo grahītuṃ yady api te rathe yuktau vāmyau syātām iti
english: The charioteer, addressed thus, said to the king: 'Do not pursue it further — this deer cannot be caught by you, even if the two Vāmya horses were yoked to your chariot.'

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd rājā sūtam ācakṣva me vāmyau hanmi vā tvām iti
english: Then the king said to the charioteer: 'Tell me about these Vāmya horses — or I will kill you!'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto rājabhayabhīto vāmadevaśāpabhītaś ca sann ācakhyau rājñe vāmadevasyāśvau vāmyau manojavāv iti
english: So addressed, he, frightened by the king's threat and fearful of Vāmadeva's curse, told the king: 'The two Vāmya horses belong to the sage Vāmadeva — they are swift as thought.'

sanskrit: athainam evaṃ bruvāṇam abravīd rājā vāmadevāśramaṃ yāhīti
english: The king then said to him as he was speaking: 'Go to Vāmadeva's hermitage!'

sanskrit: sa gatvā vāmadevāśramaṃ tam ṛṣim abravīt bhagavan mṛgo mayā viddhaḥ palāyate taṃ saṃbhāvayeyam arhasi me vāmyau dātum iti
english: Going to Vāmadeva's hermitage, he said to the sage: 'Venerable one, a deer I have wounded is fleeing; I would recover it — please grant me the two Vāmya horses.'

sanskrit: tam abravīd ṛṣiḥ dadāni te vāmyau kṛtakāryeṇa bhavatā mamaiva niryātyau kṣipram iti
english: The sage said to him: 'I will give you the two Vāmya horses; but once your purpose is accomplished, they must be promptly returned to me.'

sanskrit: sa ca tāv aśvau pratigṛhyānujñāpya carṣiṃ prāyād vāmyasaṃyuktena rathena mṛgaṃ prati gacchaṃś cābravīt sūtam aśvaratnāv imāv ayogyau brāhmaṇānām naitau pratideyau vāmadevāyeti
english: He received those two horses, took leave of the sage, and set off with the Vāmya-yoked chariot toward the deer; and as he went, he said to the charioteer: 'These two horse-gems are unfit for Brahmins — they are not to be returned to Vāmadeva.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā mṛgam avāpya svanagaram etyāśvāvantaḥpure 'sthāpayat
english: Having said this and recovered the deer, he returned to his own city and kept the horses in the inner stables.

sanskrit: atharṣiś cintayām āsa taruṇo rājaputraḥ kalyāṇaṃ patram āsādya ramate na me pratiniryātayati aho kaṣṭam iti
english: Then the sage reflected: 'This young prince, having found a fine pretext, enjoys himself and does not return them to me. Alas, how grievous!'

sanskrit: manasā niścitya māsi pūrṇe śiṣyam abravīt gacchātreya rājānaṃ brūhi yadi paryāptaṃ niryātayopādhyāyavāmyāv iti
english: Having resolved in his mind, after a month had passed he said to his disciple: 'Go, O Ātreya, and tell the king: if it has served your purpose, return the teacher's two Vāmya horses.'

sanskrit: sa gatvaivaṃ taṃ rājānam abravīt
english: He went and spoke thus to the king.

sanskrit: taṃ rājā pratyuvāca rājñām etad vāhanam anarhā brāhmaṇā ratnānām evaṃvidhānām kiṃ ca brāhmaṇānām aśvaiḥ kāryam sādhu pratigamyatām iti
english: The king replied to him: 'Such treasures as these are the mount of kings — Brahmins are not worthy of them. Besides, what need do Brahmins have of horses? Let him go away in peace.'

sanskrit: sa gatvaivam upādhyāyāyācaṣṭa
english: He went and reported thus to the teacher.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanam apriyaṃ vāmadevaḥ krodhaparītātmā svayam eva rājānam abhigamyāśvārtham abhyacodayat na cādād rājā
english: Hearing that disagreeable speech, Vāmadeva, his soul overwhelmed with anger, himself went to the king and pressed him for the horses; but the king did not give them.

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca prayaccha vāmyau mama pārthiva tvaṃ; kṛtaṃ hi te kāryam anyair aśakyam mā tvā vadhīd varuṇo ghorapāśair; brahmakṣatrasyāntare vartamānaḥ
english: Vāmadeva said: 'Return my two Vāmya horses, O king — your purpose has been accomplished, which none other could have done. Let not Varuṇa slay you with his terrible nooses, he who stands between the Brahmin and the Kṣatriya orders.'

sanskrit: rājovāca anaḍvāhau suvratau sādhu dāntāv; etad viprāṇāṃ vāhanaṃ vāmadeva tābhyāṃ yāhi tvaṃ yatra kāmo maharṣe; chandāṃsi vai tvādṛśaṃ saṃvahanti
english: The king said: 'Two well-behaved and thoroughly tamed bullocks — that is the mount of Brahmins, O Vāmadeva. On them ride wherever you wish, O great sage — Vedic meters carry the likes of you.'

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca chandāṃsi vai mādṛśaṃ saṃvahanti; loke 'muṣmin pārthiva yāni santi asmiṃs tu loke mama yānam etad; asmadvidhānām apareṣāṃ ca rājan
english: Vāmadeva said: 'Vedic meters do carry the likes of me in that other world, O king — in whatever forms they exist there. But in this world, this is my conveyance, and the conveyance of others like me, O king.'

sanskrit: rājovāca catvāro vā gardabhās tvāṃ vahantu; śreṣṭhāśvataryo harayo vā turaṃgāḥ tais tvaṃ yāhi kṣatriyasyaiṣa vāho; mama vāmyau na tavaitau hi viddhi
english: The king said: 'Let four donkeys carry you, or the finest mules, or yellow horses — on them go wherever you will. This is the mount of a Kṣatriya. Know that my two Vāmya horses are not yours.'

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca ghoraṃ vrataṃ brāhmaṇasyaitad āhur; etad rājan yad ihājīvamānaḥ ayasmayā ghorarūpā mahānto; vahantu tvāṃ śitaśūlāś caturdhā
english: Vāmadeva said: 'They call this the terrible vow of a Brahmin, O king — that one who is maintained here alive by this: let great iron demons of fearful form, with sharp spears, carry you in four directions.'

sanskrit: rājovāca ye tvā vidur brāhmaṇaṃ vāmadeva; vācā hantuṃ manasā karmaṇā vā te tvāṃ saśiṣyam iha pātayantu; madvākyanunnāḥ śitaśūlāsihastāḥ
english: The king said: 'Those who know you as a Brahmin capable of slaying with word, mind, or deed — let them cast you down here together with your disciples, driven by my command, bearing sharp spears and swords.'

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca nānuyogā brāhmaṇānāṃ bhavanti; vācā rājan manasā karmaṇā vā yas tv evaṃ brahma tapasānveti vidvāṃs; tena śreṣṭho bhavati hi jīvamānaḥ
english: Vāmadeva said: 'No sanctions constrain Brahmins, O king — neither by word, nor by mind, nor by deed. But one who thus pursues Brahmā-knowledge through austerity, knowing it fully, by that he becomes the highest while he lives.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam ukte vāmadevena rājan; samuttasthū rākṣasā ghorarūpāḥ taiḥ śūlahastair vadhyamānaḥ sa rājā; provācedaṃ vākyam uccais tadānīm
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: 'O king, when Vāmadeva had spoken thus, rākṣasas of fearsome form rose up; being struck down by them — spear in hand — that king then cried out these words aloud:

sanskrit: ikṣvākavo yadi brahman dalo vā; vidheyā me yadi vānye viśo 'pi notsrakṣye 'haṃ vāmadevasya vāmyau; naivaṃvidhā dharmaśīlā bhavanti
english: "O Brahmin, whether the Ikṣvākus, or Dala, are subject to me, or even other common folk — I will not release Vāmadeva's two Vāmya horses. Those of dharmic character do not act in such a way."'

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvann eva sa yātudhānair; hato jagāmāśu mahīṃ kṣitīśaḥ tato viditvā nṛpatiṃ nipātitam; ikṣvākavo vai dalam abhyaṣiñcan
english: Speaking thus, that lord of the earth was slain by the demons and fell quickly to the ground. Then, knowing the king to be slain, the Ikṣvākus consecrated Dala as king.

sanskrit: rājye tadā tatra gatvā sa vipraḥ; provācedaṃ vacanaṃ vāmadevaḥ dalaṃ rājānaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ hi deyam; evaṃ rājan sarvadharmeṣu dṛṣṭam
english: Then the Brahmin Vāmadeva, going there into the kingdom, spoke these words: 'Dala, O king, what belongs to Brahmins must be given — this is seen as such in all the codes of dharma.'

sanskrit: bibheṣi cet tvam adharmān narendra; prayaccha me śīghram evādya vāmyau etac chrutvā vāmadevasya vākyaṃ; sa pārthivaḥ sūtam uvāca roṣāt
english: 'If you fear unrighteousness, O lord of men, give me the two Vāmya horses right now today.' Hearing these words of Vāmadeva, that king spoke to his charioteer in fury:

sanskrit: ekaṃ hi me sāyakaṃ citrarūpaṃ; digdhaṃ viṣeṇāhara saṃgṛhītam yena viddho vāmadevaḥ śayīta; saṃdaśyamānaḥ śvabhir ārtarūpaḥ
english: 'Bring me at once one of my arrows of peculiar form, smeared with poison and ready to hand — one by which Vāmadeva, when struck, may lie down, mauled by dogs in a pitiful state.'

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca jānāmi putraṃ daśavarṣaṃ tavāhaṃ; jātaṃ mahiṣyāṃ śyenajitaṃ narendra taṃ jahi tvaṃ madvacanāt praṇunnas; tūrṇaṃ priyaṃ sāyakair ghorarūpaiḥ
english: Vāmadeva said: 'I know, O lord of men, your son ten years of age, born of the queen — named Śyenajit. Him, driven by my command, slay promptly, your own dear one, with dreadful arrows.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam ukto vāmadevena rājann; antaḥpure rājaputraṃ jaghāna sa sāyakas tigmatejā visṛṣṭaḥ; śrutvā dalas tac ca vākyaṃ babhāṣe
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: 'O king, addressed thus by Vāmadeva, the arrow, blazing with sharp power, was released and slew the prince in the inner chamber. Hearing this, Dala also spoke these words:

sanskrit: ikṣvākavo hanta carāmi vaḥ priyaṃ; nihanmīmaṃ vipram adya pramathya ānīyatām aparas tigmatejāḥ; paśyadhvaṃ me vīryam adya kṣitīśāḥ
english: "O Ikṣvākus, behold — I shall do what is dear to you; today I shall smite and kill this Brahmin. Bring me another blazing sharp arrow — O lords of earth, behold my valor today!"'

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca yaṃ tvam enaṃ sāyakaṃ ghorarūpaṃ; viṣeṇa digdhaṃ mama saṃdadhāsi na tvam enaṃ śaravaryaṃ vimoktuṃ; saṃdhātuṃ vā śakṣyasi mānavendra
english: Vāmadeva said: 'That terrible arrow, smeared with poison, which you are now fitting against me — you will not be able to release that best of arrows or even to nock it, O lord of men.'

sanskrit: rājovāca ikṣvākavaḥ paśyata māṃ gṛhītaṃ; na vai śaknomy eṣa śaraṃ vimoktum na cāsya kartuṃ nāśam abhyutsahāmi; āyuṣmān vai jīvatu vāmadevaḥ
english: The king said: 'O Ikṣvākus, look — I am seized! Truly I cannot release this arrow, nor can I bring myself to destroy it. Let Vāmadeva live long!'

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca saṃspṛśaināṃ mahiṣīṃ sāyakena; tatas tasmād enaso mokṣyase tvam
english: Vāmadeva said: 'Touch the queen with this arrow — from that sin you will be released.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tatas tathā kṛtavān pārthivas tu; tato muniṃ rājaputrī babhāṣe yathā yuktaṃ vāmadevāham enaṃ; dine dine saṃviśantī vyaśaṃsam brāhmaṇebhyo mṛgayantī sūnṛtāni; tathā brahman puṇyalokaṃ labheyam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: 'The king then did as instructed. Then the princess spoke to the sage: "O Vāmadeva, as befits the situation, I, spending each day united with him, have praised him to Brahmins, ever seeking kind words — may I thereby, O Brahmin, attain the world of merit."'

sanskrit: vāmadeva uvāca tvayā trātaṃ rājakulaṃ śubhekṣaṇe; varaṃ vṛṇīṣvāpratimaṃ dadāni te praśādhīmaṃ svajanaṃ rājaputri; ikṣvākurājyaṃ sumahac cāpy anindye
english: Vāmadeva said: 'You have saved the royal family, O bright-eyed one. Choose a matchless boon — I grant it to you. Rule over your own kindred, O princess — and also over the great and blameless Ikṣvāku kingdom.'

sanskrit: rājaputry uvāca varaṃ vṛṇe bhagavann ekam eva; vimucyatāṃ kilbiṣād adya bhartā śivena cādhyāhi saputrabāndhavaṃ; varo vṛto hy eṣa mayā dvijāgrya
english: The princess said: 'I choose but one boon, O Lord — let my husband be freed today from his sin. Bless him together with his sons and kinsmen with auspiciousness. This is the boon I have chosen, O foremost of twice-born ones.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca śrutvā vacaḥ sa munī rājaputryās; tathāstv iti prāha kurupravīra tataḥ sa rājā mudito babhūva; vāmyau cāsmai saṃpradadau praṇamya
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: 'Hearing the princess's words, O foremost of Kurus, the sage said, "So be it." Then the king became joyful, and bowing, he gave the two Vāmya horses to him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca mārkaṇḍeyam ṛṣayaḥ pāṇḍavāś ca paryapṛcchan asti kaś cid bhavataś cirajātatara iti
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The sages and the Pāṇḍavas questioned Mārkaṇḍeya: 'Is there anyone elder than yourself?'

sanskrit: sa tān uvāca asti khalu rājarṣir indradyumno nāma kṣīṇapuṇyas tridivāt pracyutaḥ kīrtis te vyucchinneti sa mām upātiṣṭhat atha pratyabhijānāti māṃ bhavān iti
english: He said to them: 'Indeed there was a royal sage named Indradyumna whose merit was exhausted and who fell from the triple heaven with the words: "Your fame has been cut off." He came to me and asked: "Do you, sir, know me?"'

sanskrit: tam aham abruvam na vayaṃ rāsāyanikāḥ śarīropatāpenātmanaḥ samārabhāmahe 'rthānām anuṣṭhānam
english: 'I said to him: "We are not alchemists who undertake the accomplishment of our purposes through torment of the body."

sanskrit: asti khalu himavati prākārakarṇo nāmolūkaḥ sa bhavantaṃ yadi jānīyāt prakṛṣṭe cādhvani himavān tatrāsau prativasatīti
english: '"There is on the Himālayas an owl named Prākārakarṇa — if he might know you. The Himālaya is at a great distance; there that one dwells."'

sanskrit: sa mām aśvo bhūtvā tatrāvahad yatra babhūvolūkaḥ
english: 'He, having become a horse, carried me there where the owl was.'

sanskrit: athainaṃ sa rājarṣiḥ paryapṛcchat pratyabhijānāti māṃ bhavān iti
english: 'Then that royal sage questioned him: "Do you know me, sir?"'

sanskrit: sa muhūrtaṃ dhyātvābravīd enam nābhijāne bhavantam iti
english: 'He, meditating for a moment, said to him: "I do not know you, sir."'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto rājarṣir indradyumnaḥ punas tam ulūkam abravīt asti kaś cid bhavataś cirajātatara iti
english: 'The royal sage Indradyumna, thus addressed, again said to that owl: "Is there anyone elder than yourself?"'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto 'bravīd enam asti khalv indradyumnasaro nāma tasmin nāḍījaṅgho nāma bakaḥ prativasati so 'smattaś cirajātataraḥ taṃ pṛccheti
english: 'Addressed thus, he said to him: "Indeed there is a lake called Indradyumna-saras; in it a heron named Nāḍījaṅgha dwells — he is elder than I. Ask him."'

sanskrit: tata indradyumno māṃ colūkaṃ cādāya tat saro 'gacchad yatrāsau nāḍījaṅgho nāma bako babhūva
english: 'Then Indradyumna, taking me and the owl, went to that lake where the heron named Nāḍījaṅgha was.'

sanskrit: so 'smābhiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ bhavān indradyumnaṃ rājānaṃ pratyabhijānātīti
english: 'He was asked by us: "Do you, sir, know King Indradyumna?"'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto 'bravīn muhūrtaṃ dhyātvā nābhijānāmy aham indradyumnaṃ rājānam iti
english: 'So addressed, he reflected for a moment and said: "I do not know King Indradyumna."'

sanskrit: tataḥ so 'smābhiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ asti kaś cid anyo bhavataś cirajātatara iti
english: 'Then he was asked by us: "Is there anyone else elder than yourself?"'

sanskrit: sa no 'bravīd asti khalv ihaiva sarasy akūpāro nāma kacchapaḥ prativasati sa mattaś cirajātatara iti sa yadi kathaṃ cid abhijānīyād imaṃ rājānaṃ tam akūpāraṃ pṛcchāma iti
english: 'He said to us: "Indeed, in this very lake there lives a tortoise named Akūpāra — he is elder than I. If he could perhaps recognize this king, we should ask that Akūpāra."'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bakas tam akūpāraṃ kacchapaṃ vijñāpayām āsa asty asmākam abhipretaṃ bhavantaṃ kaṃ cid artham abhipraṣṭum sādhv āgamyatāṃ tāvad iti
english: 'Then the heron informed the tortoise Akūpāra: "We have a purpose in mind — we wish to ask you something; please come here for a moment."'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā sa kacchapas tasmāt sarasa utthāyābhyagacchad yatra tiṣṭhāmo vayaṃ tasya sarasas tīre
english: 'Hearing this, the tortoise rose from that lake and came to where we were standing on the bank of that lake.'

sanskrit: āgataṃ cainaṃ vayam apṛcchāma bhavān indyadyumnaṃ rājānam abhijānātīti
english: 'And when he had come, we asked him: "Do you, sir, know King Indradyumna?"'

sanskrit: sa muhūrtaṃ dhyātvā bāṣpapūrṇanayana udvignahṛdayo vepamāno visaṃjñakalpaḥ prāñjalir abravīt kim aham enaṃ na pratyabhijānāmi ahaṃ hy anena sahasrakṛtvaḥ pūrvam agnicitiṣūpahitapūrvaḥ saraś cedam asya dakṣiṇādattābhir gobhir atikramamāṇābhiḥ kṛtam atra cāhaṃ prativasāmīti
english: 'He, meditating for a moment, his eyes filled with tears, his heart agitated, trembling, nearly senseless, with joined palms said: "How could I not know him? For he had previously offered me as a gift a thousand times in fire-altar sacrifices; and this lake was made by the cows given as gifts at his southern rites when they passed over the land; and here I have been living."'

sanskrit: athaitat kacchapenodāhṛtaṃ śrutvā samanantaraṃ devalokād devarathaḥ prādurāsīt
english: 'Then, immediately upon hearing what was spoken by the tortoise, a divine chariot appeared from the world of the gods.'

sanskrit: vācaś cāśrūyantendradyumnaṃ prati prastutas te svargaḥ yathocitaṃ sthānam abhipadyasva kīrtimān asi avyagro yāhīti
english: 'And voices were heard addressed to Indradyumna: "Your heaven is ready — occupy the station that befits you. You are glorious. Go without anxiety."'

sanskrit: divaṃ spṛśati bhūmiṃ ca śabdaḥ puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ yāvat sa śabdo bhavati tāvat puruṣa ucyate
english: 'The renown of meritorious deeds touches both heaven and earth; as long as that fame endures, so long is a man spoken of.'

sanskrit: akīrtiḥ kīrtyate yasya loke bhūtasya kasya cit pataty evādhamāṃl lokān yāvac chabdaḥ sa kīrtyate
english: 'One whose ill-fame is spoken of in the world — whatever being it may be — falls into the lowest realms for as long as that utterance continues to be spoken.'

sanskrit: tasmāt kalyāṇavṛttaḥ syād atyantāya naro bhuvi vihāya vṛttaṃ pāpiṣṭhaṃ dharmam evābhisaṃśrayet
english: 'Therefore a man should be of virtuous conduct in the world to the utmost degree; abandoning sinful conduct, he should take refuge in dharma alone.'

sanskrit: ity etac chrutvā sa rājābravīt tiṣṭha tāvad yāvad idānīm imau vṛddhau yathāsthānaṃ pratipādayāmīti
english: 'Hearing this, the king said: "Wait a moment while I restore these two elders to their proper places."'

sanskrit: sa māṃ prākārakarṇaṃ colūkaṃ yathocite sthāne pratipādya tenaiva yānena saṃsiddho yathocitaṃ sthānaṃ pratipannaḥ
english: 'He restored me, Prākārakarṇa, and the owl each to their proper places, and then, his purpose accomplished, took that same vehicle and attained his rightful station.'

sanskrit: etan mayānubhūtaṃ cirajīvinā dṛṣṭam iti pāṇḍavān uvāca mārkaṇḍeyaḥ
english: 'This was experienced and witnessed by me as a long-liver' — so Mārkaṇḍeya said to the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś cocuḥ prītāḥ sādhu śobhanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavatā rājānam indradyumnaṃ svargalokāc cyutaṃ sve sthāne svarge punaḥ pratipādayateti
english: The Pāṇḍavas, pleased, said: 'Well done — it is excellent that you restored King Indradyumna, who had fallen from the heavenly world, once again to his own place in heaven.'

sanskrit: athainān abravīd asau nanu devakīputreṇāpi kṛṣṇena narake majjamāno rājarṣir nṛgas tasmāt kṛcchrāt samuddhṛtya punaḥ svargaṃ pratipādita iti
english: Then he said to them: 'Moreover, was not the royal sage Nṛga, sinking in hell, rescued from that dire state by Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī, and again restored to heaven?'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yudhiṣṭhiro dharmarājaḥ papraccha bharatarṣabha mārkaṇḍeyaṃ tapovṛddhaṃ dīrghāyuṣam akalmaṣam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Yudhiṣṭhira, the dharma-king, O bull of the Bhārata lineage, questioned Mārkaṇḍeya — great through austerities, long-lived, and without blemish.

sanskrit: viditās tava dharmajña devadānavarākṣasāḥ rājavaṃśāś ca vividhā ṛṣivaṃśāś ca śāśvatāḥ na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cid asmiṃl loke dvijottama
english: 'Known to you, O knower of dharma, are the gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas; the various royal lineages and the eternal sages' lineages — nothing in this world is unknown to you, O foremost of the twice-born.'
